doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Eli's Chosen Six, the Gotham Jazz Men and the band's humor
summary: Sherman compares the all-volunteer All-Stars to Yale's paid Eli's Chosen Six, mentions Lee Lorenz and the Gotham Jazz Men, and tells how the band's humor shows in the private-bathroom emails.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yup. There is a band that has played almost as long, Eli’s Chosen Six from Yale. But I play with some of those guys all the time and they do not donate any jazz to their alma mater, they play less frequently and they are paid, and extremely well paid for their work.
Wow. You know Roswell Rudd, the trombone player, mentioned that group.
That he played with them I think.

Well I specifically talked about Dick Voight, who is the piano player, who helped me take the survey so I could make the claim that we are the longest playing band, and the cornet player was Lee Lorenz, who is the cartoonist for the New Yorker, a multi-talented man, he’s also a writer, and he plays in my Manhattan band, the Gotham Jazz Men. And we play every Thursday, a noontime concert free, and thirty plus years. We are in our thirty-first year donating that jazz. And I heard Phil say, in response to your question, is how come people’s chops are in shape and why are they up to snuff when they come here? Well we each have our own local band, such as the Gotham Jazz Men in Manhattan in which Lee Lorenz plays cornet. And that keeps us on top of our game. So they’re all
around the country playing in their local bands, then they convene at Hamilton and then we really have fun.
Yeah. And you guys do have fun.

We have fun, and the band is a bunch of humorists. They’re very, very funny. I’ve played in many bands, Monk, over the years. This bunch, every one of them is a live wire. They’re funny. We exchange emails and mailings and they’re always hilarious, on any subject. For instance, Donny Andre, our banjoist, wanted to be sure that when we take up our residence for this next few days in an ex-fraternity house, that we would each have a private bathroom. And by George that was very difficult for Laurie Russell, our Alumni Affairs honcho, to arrange. But she said, “I’ll keep trying.” And I kept hearing from Donny Andre, “Are we going to get our private bathrooms?” Well finally at the last minute she said, “You’re going to be in the old Psi U house, which is known as the Skenandoa House, and guess what, you’re getting private loos, each one will have one. So I announced this to the members of the band in a poem called “A Private Loo,” and they seemed to enjoy it. That’s the thing. We don’t require anything fancy or anything particularly noteworthy to be a subject for humor.
